translate_en|mods/TrampleSteam/42/media/: On (default): launched animals die when they land. Off: they survive the flight, indignant but unharmed.
On (default): launching an animal wears the trap down like a zombie launch does. Off: flinging the chickens is free.
Guaranteed launches before the mechanism starts wearing out. Past that, every launch rolls the Jam chance below. Set to 999 for an unbreakable trap.
Off (default): deploying a Trample Steam requires Mechanics 2, a technical occupation (Engineer, Electrician, Mechanic, Metalworker), or having read the magazine. On: anyone can deploy one.
If on (default), launched survivors blurt something out mid-flight. Turn off for a silent, dignified somersault.
If on (default), an armed trap quietly hums (audible only a few tiles away, and only while it has fuel in gasoline mode).
If on, the trap re-arms in a quarter of a second (the swing animation still plays). If off, it takes the Reset time below before it can fire again.
Once a trap has used up its charges it keeps working, but every further launch has this chance to jam the mechanism. Default 20. At 0 a worn trap never jams.
On (default): livestock and wildlife that wander onto the pad get launched too. Whether the flight kills them and whether it wears the trap are the two options below.
Multiplies how far and how high victims are flung. 1 (default) is the normal spring; 0.5 is a polite shove, 4 is a catapult.
On (default): the launch bang, the ready ding and the idle hum are real noise that draws nearby zombies toward the trap, so it baits its own victims. Off: the sounds are audible to you only.
Who can pack up a trap

Who is allowed to pack up (or scrap) a deployed Trample Steam. 'Owner + allies' extends it to the owner's faction members and anyone sharing a safehouse with them; 'Owner only' limits it to whoever deployed that trap, so rivals can't steal your defenses in PvP. Admins and the build cheat always can. Default: everyone.

Off (default): a launched survivor can take falling damage on a hard landing, especially at high Launch power. On: trap launches never deal fall damage, so pads can be chained into a launch-transit network across the map.

Extra health a survivor loses when the trap launches them. 0 (the default) adds nothing, though a rough landing can still hurt a little depending on the launch angle and how you come down. Raise it to make stepping on your own trap properly dangerous.

Who the trap will launch besides zombies. 'Everyone but the owner' uses the name of whoever deployed the trap. 'Everyone but the owner's allies' also spares the owner's faction members and anyone sharing a safehouse with them: allies walk over the pad safely, raiders fly.
If on, launching a survivor wears the trap down like a zombie launch does. Off (default): bouncing players is free.

What powers the trap. Gasoline: deploys empty, refuel from a gas can, sips roughly one tank per week. Generator/grid: runs while the tile has electricity (a powered building or a running generator nearby). Both (default): runs if EITHER fuel or electricity is available. None: always powered.

Quickly switch the trap between play styles. 'Custom' uses the individual settings below as-is. 'Co-op PvE / Singleplayer' pins the recommended cooperative values (free harmless player launches, nothing restricted, no sabotage). 'Co-op PvE / Singleplayer Casual' is that plus safe landings, deployment as global knowledge, and traps that never need fuel or power. 'PvP' makes launches hit everyone for 35 damage and use a charge, turns off the mid-flight remarks, restricts pack-up, siphoning and upgrades to the owner and their faction/safehouse allies, and enables sabotage. Settings the preset doesn't cover still come from this page. Server admins can flip this live from the Sandbox Options panel; it applies within a minute, no restart needed.

On (default): launched victims react like they were hit by a car, ragdolling as physics ragdolls (this forces the game's 'Use Physics Hit Reaction' display option on). Every victim leaves on its own slightly-off heading with its own tumble, and touchdown is a couple of shrinking bounces and a short skid, with a fresh ragdoll kick at each impact. Note: the game disables ragdoll physics in multiplayer (just like real car hits), so multiplayer uses the regular falldown animations. Off: victims are launched in a normal pose, land once and stop.

Off (default): the crafting recipe must be learned from the 'How to Use: Trample Steam' magazine (spawns as rarely as the generator magazine); Engineers and Metalworkers know it from the start. On: everyone knows the recipe.
Guaranteed launches after reinforcing a trap with extra sheet metal (context menu, needs welding gear). Set to 999 to make reinforced traps unbreakable.
Seconds the trap needs to re-cock and re-arm after firing, and to arm itself when first deployed (used only when Instant reset is off). Default 7.

Off (default): deployed traps can't be tampered with. On: any survivor with a screwdriver and Electrical 2 can attempt to jam a deployed Trample Steam. Success quietly breaks it (repairable as usual); a botched attempt makes a loud clank that draws zombies. Higher Electrical skill improves the odds. PvP counter-play against enemy trap lines.
Who can siphon gasoline from a trap

Who is allowed to siphon stored gasoline back out of a deployed trap into a gas can. 'Owner + allies' extends it to the owner's faction members and anyone sharing a safehouse with them; 'Owner only' stops fuel theft in PvP; 'Nobody' makes fueling a one-way trip. Admins and the build cheat always can. Default: everyone.

Scales how far every trap sound carries -- the launch bang, the re-cock ratchet, the ready ding, the idle hum and the landing thud -- and equally how far away zombies can hear them (when Noise attracts zombies is on). The sounds keep their relative loudness; only the reach changes. 1 = the default curve, 0.1 = barely past the pad, 4 = the whole neighborhood hears it.
Short delay between something stepping on the pad and the launch, letting more zombies pile on so one charge flings the whole group. Default 0.07; set to 0 to fire instantly.

Who is allowed to upgrade a deployed Trample Steam -- one setting covers all three upgrades: Reinforcing, Camouflage and Spring tuning. 'Owner + allies' extends it to the owner's faction members and anyone sharing a safehouse with them; 'Owner only' stops rivals from re-skinning or de-tuning your defenses in PvP. Admins and the build cheat always can. On top of this, upgrading always needs the deployment know-how (Mechanics 2, a technical occupation, or the magazine). Default: everyone.
On (default): launched zombies die when they land. Off: they survive the flight and get back up. Launch them into another trap for zombie pinball.
If on, the trap re-arms in a quarter of a second (the swing animation still plays). If off, it takes the Reset time below and plays the full reset animation.
Health a survivor loses when the trap launches them (0 = harmless bounce, the default).

On (default): victims are flung as physics ragdolls with per-victim scatter, tumble, bounces and a skid (forces the game's physics-hit-reaction on). Off: they're launched in a normal pose and die on landing.
Seconds to re-arm after firing (when Instant reset is off). Default 7.
Scales how far every trap sound carries, and how far away zombies can hear them. 1 = default, 0.1 = barely past the pad, 4 = the whole neighborhood.
Puts a spring in your step. Parachute not included.
